text: The standard contemporary resolution of the paradox of the stone ("Can God create a stone too heavy for him to lift?") holds that:
choices: creating a stone that an omnipotent being cannot lift is not a genuine task at all, like drawing a round square, so failing to do it is no limit on omnipotence.
God can do absolutely anything, including the logically impossible, so God can both create such a stone and then lift it.
omnipotence should be given up in favor of the view that God merely 'lures' creatures toward the good without coercive power.
God's inability to sin already shows that omnipotence is compatible with there being some things God cannot do.
explanation: The standard modal resolution restricts omnipotence to intrinsically possible states of affairs; a stone too heavy for an omnipotent being to lift is an incoherent description—no task at all—so it sets no limit on power. Distractor 1 is Descartes's universal possibilism (God can do even the logically impossible), a real but widely rejected view, not the standard resolution.
